guide.title: Black Desert Resort: Golf in Ivins, Utah
guide.intro: Golf Digest's 2025-'26 Best in State ranking places Black Desert Resort second in Utah, carrying Golf Digest's own "Public" label. Glenwild Golf Club & Spa is ranked #1 in Utah on the same list, where it carries Golf Digest's "Private" label; skipping only that one entry, Black Desert Resort is the highest-ranked course on the list carrying the "Public" label. Golf Digest calls Black Desert Resort "the last golf course Tom Weiskopf was involved in building." The course sits at 1500 E Black Desert Dr, Ivins, in Washington County, Utah — a different place from Washington City, a separate municipality also inside Washington County. Black Desert Resort's own 2026 Course Conditions calendar closes the course to all play from September 14 through October 6, 2026, while it hosts the PGA TOUR's Black Desert Championship and completes tournament preparations; anyone planning a visit around those dates should check the operator's calendar first, and the closure is repeated in the FAQ below.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body: St. George Regional Airport (SGU) is the closest airport, 20 miles from the resort's front gate, in the resort's own words. Black Desert Resort is seven miles from St. George, Utah, also stated by the resort itself. Las Vegas and Salt Lake City are the resort's named connecting airports; the resort states only drive times for each, not a mileage, so neither figure is published here. The resort's own Getting Here page gives no road numbers for the final approach — only map links — so none is stated here. Cvent's venue record for the resort, a directory listing rather than the operator's own page, gives Snow Canyon State Park as 1 mile away, Tuacahn Amphitheatre as 2 miles away, Kayenta Art Village as 4 miles away, Sand Hollow State Park — home of the day-two course below — as 19 miles away, Zion National Park as 39 miles away, and Bryce Canyon National Park as 131 miles away.

sections.heading: Playing Black Desert as a public golfer
sections.body: Black Desert Resort's golf course closes to all play from September 14 through October 6, 2026, while it hosts the PGA TOUR's Black Desert Championship and completes tournament preparations, per the resort's own 2026 Course Conditions table. Outside that window, the course is open to non-members: book by phone at 435-222-7830, or online. The resort's own FAQ answer reads, "Please call the Golf Shop 435-222-7830, or book your tee time online!" and links to Chronogolf, the resort's booking system. Chronogolf's own club record for Black Desert Resort carries a public booking window: "Public players can book up to 30 days in advance at this course." Staying on property is optional: the resort publishes a standing Non-Resort Guest rate alongside its Resort Guest rate, and the FAQ's booking instructions attach no lodging condition — staying on property changes only the price, not whether you can book. Chronogolf's booking system also restricts single-player online bookings, so a solo golfer should call the Golf Shop rather than count on booking online.

sections.heading: The course
sections.body: The PGA Tour describes the layout as "the par-72 Black Desert Golf Course was designed by Phil Smith and the late Tom Weiskopf"; Golf Digest independently credits Phil Smith, "Weiskopf's longtime design partner," with completing "the visually arresting design" after Weiskopf was diagnosed with cancer as construction began. It is Weiskopf's final design, completed by Smith. The course opened in 2023 — May 2023, per GolfPass. It plays to par 72 over 7,500 yards across 18 holes, plus what the operator calls "a bonus 19th hole for bet settling." The PGA TOUR's Black Desert Championship debuted here in the fall of 2024; the resort's own FAQ records that "the first edition was held in October 2024 and won by Matt McCarty." Golf Digest calls it "the first tour event in Utah in more than 60 years." An LPGA Black Desert Championship followed in May 2025.

sections.heading: Green fees and the 2026 calendar
sections.body: Black Desert Resort's own rate table, current through January 1, 2027, publishes four dated 2026 bands. Resort Guest pays $250 from January 2 to March 12 and again from July 7 to September 3, and $325 from March 13 to July 6 and from September 4, 2026 to January 1, 2027. Non-Resort Guest pays $325 in the same two lower bands and $450 in the same two higher bands. For July 7 through September 3, the resort's own footnote states that the listed, lower summer rates apply to tee times from 10:15 a.m. through close, while tee times between 7:00 and 10:00 a.m. are charged at the higher peak-season rates. Rates include green fees, a golf cart, a forecaddie, and food and non-alcoholic beverages at Oasis and Club 73 while golfing, plus access to practice facilities and a keepsake; the resort's FAQ adds dedicated CADDIEMASTER forecaddies and carts capable of fifteen miles per hour. Beyond the rate table, the same 2026 Course Conditions calendar sets cart-path-only restrictions during spring aerification recovery from February 26 to March 12, limited tee access during PGA Tour preparations from August 1 to September 13, and closure to all play from September 14 to October 6 while the PGA TOUR event is played and torn down.

sections.heading: The resort
sections.body: Black Desert Resort's on-property lodging is organized into named collections: Hotel Collection, Plume Wellness Collection, Resort Collection, The Terrace Collection, and The Cove Collection, the last of which the resort itself marks "Coming Soon." The resort's FAQ puts the total at "nearly 800 rooms and suites"; a Cvent venue record for the resort independently gives 791 guest rooms. The resort names seven restaurants in its own site navigation: Basalt ("Elevated Americana"), Latitude ("Baja-California Inspired"), 20th Hole ("Sports Bar"), Flo ("Meet in the Lobby"), Lava Love ("Coffee & More"), Oasis ("Southwestern Fare... A Mexican taqueria-inspired menu"), and Club 73 ("Open-Air Dining... backyard barbecue"). What the sources establish is that these rooms and restaurants exist and what they are named and described as; none of them says whether any given room or restaurant is serving this week, so this guide does not say so either.

sections.heading: Day two: Sand Hollow
sections.body: The second course to play is Sand Hollow Resort: Championship Course, tenth on the same Golf Digest Utah list and also labelled "Public." It sits in Hurricane, which the county's own list of its cities also places in Washington County, Utah, alongside Ivins. John Fought and Andy Staples designed it, and it opened in 2008. Sand Hollow's own booking page states: "Reservations may be made up to 180 days in advance. A credit card number is required to make a reservation. Cancellations and player reductions must be done at least 48 hours in advance." It adds that "Single players may book within 48 hours by calling the Pro Shop." No resort-guest-priority language appears on that page.

faq.question: How do I book a tee time at Black Desert?
faq.answer: Call the Golf Shop at 435-222-7830, or book online through Chronogolf, the system the resort's own FAQ names — its answer reads, "Please call the Golf Shop 435-222-7830, or book your tee time online!" Chronogolf's own club record for the resort sets a public booking window of 30 days ahead. You do not have to stay on property to book: the resort publishes a standing Non-Resort Guest rate alongside its Resort Guest rate, with no lodging condition attached to the booking instructions. Before you book: the course is closed to all play from September 14 through October 6, 2026, while it hosts the PGA TOUR's Black Desert Championship and completes tournament preparations.

faq.question: Is the course open right now?
faq.answer: Not on every date. Black Desert Resort's own 2026 Course Conditions table closes the course to all play from September 14 through October 6, 2026, for the PGA TOUR event and its teardown. The same table also sets cart-path-only restrictions during spring aerification recovery, February 26 to March 12, and limited tee access during PGA Tour preparations, August 1 to September 13. Check the operator's own calendar before planning a visit.

faq.question: Do I have to book a room to play?
faq.answer: No. The resort publishes a standing Non-Resort Guest green fee alongside its Resort Guest rate, and its FAQ's booking instructions — call the Golf Shop or book online — attach no lodging condition. Staying on property changes only the price, not whether you can book.

faq.question: Can I book online if I'm playing alone?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Chronogolf, the resort's own booking system, restricts single-player online bookings, so a solo golfer should call the Golf Shop at 435-222-7830 rather than count on booking online.

faq.question: What does a round cost?
faq.answer: From Black Desert Resort's own rate table, current through January 1, 2027: Resort Guest pays $250 from January 2 to March 12 and again from July 7 to September 3, and $325 from March 13 to July 6 and from September 4, 2026 to January 1, 2027. Non-Resort Guest pays $325 in the same two lower bands and $450 in the same two higher bands. For July 7 through September 3, the resort's own footnote states that the listed, lower summer rates apply to tee times from 10:15 a.m. through close, while tee times between 7:00 and 10:00 a.m. are charged at the higher peak-season rates.

faq.question: Who designed the course?
faq.answer: The PGA Tour: "the par-72 Black Desert Golf Course was designed by Phil Smith and the late Tom Weiskopf." Golf Digest independently credits Phil Smith, "Weiskopf's longtime design partner," with completing "the visually arresting design" after Weiskopf was diagnosed with cancer as construction began. It is Weiskopf's final design, completed by Smith.

faq.question: Where is Black Desert Resort?
faq.answer: At 1500 E Black Desert Dr, Ivins, UT 84738, in Washington County, Utah. Ivins is a separate municipality from Washington City, which is also inside Washington County; the course is in Ivins, not Washington City.

faq.question: Which course should I play on day two?
faq.answer: Sand Hollow Resort: Championship Course, tenth on the same Golf Digest Utah list and also labelled "Public," in Hurricane, also within Washington County, Utah. John Fought and Andy Staples designed it and it opened in 2008. Its own booking page states reservations may be made up to 180 days in advance, a credit card is required, cancellations and player reductions need at least 48 hours' notice, and single players may book within 48 hours by calling the Pro Shop.
